page: Google Cloud Platform m4-ultramem-224 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the m4 family. It features 224 dedicated virtual CPUs and 5952.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of approximately 26.57 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include integrated GPUs or local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached storage options.

Designed for memory-intensive workloads, the instance provides massive RAM capacity to keep large datasets entirely in-memory. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent compute performance across all 224 vCPUs. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware profile represents a highly specialized resource density optimized for massive memory footprints, reducing the need to distribute databases across multiple smaller nodes and simplifying cluster management.

The m4-ultramem-224 is engineered for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, massive data analytics pipelines, and memory-heavy enterprise workloads that require substantial RAM without the need for local physical disks or GPU acceleration.
